description.summary: A 5 V low-voltage LED oscillator built around an 8-pin timer/control device. The circuit contains a resistive-capacitive timing network and an LED output branch.
description.intended_behaviour: With no planted fault, TP_OUTPUT changes between low and high states at approximately one cycle per second and LED1 visibly blinks.

components.description: timing resistor from TP_SUPPLY to the discharge-side timing node
timing resistor between the discharge-side timing node and TP_TIMING
timing capacitor between TP_TIMING and GND
LED current-limiting resistor between TP_OUTPUT and LED1
polarity-sensitive indicator LED connected from R3 to GND
reset-node pull-up resistor between TP_SUPPLY and TP_RESET

connections: The circuit is powered from TP_SUPPLY and GND.
R1 connects TP_SUPPLY to the discharge-side timing node.
R2 connects the discharge-side timing node to TP_TIMING.
TP_OUTPUT connects through R3 and LED1 to GND.
LED1's anode faces R3 and its cathode faces GND in the intended orientation.
observable_features: whether LED1 is dark, continuously on, or visibly blinking
visible disconnected conductors or damaged joints
user-reported multimeter measurements at the defined test points

test_points.description: 5 V supply rail measured relative to GND
reset/control node measured relative to GND
output node measured relative to GND
capacitor timing node measured relative to GND

available_tests.procedure: Use only this 5 V demo board. If you cannot locate TP_SUPPLY and GND, stop and ask for help identifying them. Before connecting the probes, put the black lead in COM and the red lead in the voltage (V) socket, not a current socket. Select DC voltage (V with a straight/dashed line); use auto-range or a manual range above 5.5 V, such as 20 V. With the board powered from its specified 5 V DC supply, touch the black probe to GND and the red probe to TP_SUPPLY. Keep the tips from bridging adjacent contacts. Report the displayed voltage, including its sign and unit.

possible_results.implication: The expected input supply is absent or nearly absent at TP_SUPPLY. Downstream timing, output, or LED faults cannot by themselves explain the missing board supply.
The board supply is below the recorded 4.5 V to 5.5 V operating range. Supply-path loss or excessive loading must be considered before normal downstream behaviour is assumed.
The board input supply is within the recorded operating range. Complete loss of input supply is not supported by this measurement.
The board supply is above the recorded operating range. The supply condition must be resolved before downstream behaviour is interpreted as normal.

available_tests.procedure: Use only this 5 V demo board. If you cannot locate TP_RESET and GND, stop and ask for help identifying them. Before connecting the probes, put the black lead in COM and the red lead in the voltage (V) socket, not a current socket. Select DC voltage (V with a straight/dashed line); use auto-range or a manual range above 5.5 V, such as 20 V. With the board powered from its specified 5 V DC supply, touch the black probe to GND and the red probe to TP_RESET. Keep the tips from bridging adjacent contacts. Report the displayed voltage, including its sign and unit.

possible_results.implication: TP_RESET is near GND rather than the intended supply level. A reset-path fault is a hypothesis; exact reset assertion depends on the actual device threshold.
TP_RESET is neither in the defined low range nor near the 5 V supply rail. This measurement does not establish whether the reset path is operating normally.
A reset node held low is not supported by this measurement, so a low-reset condition becomes less likely as the cause of the observed symptom.
TP_RESET is above the circuit's recorded operating supply range. The supply and measurement conditions must be checked before the reset state is interpreted.

available_tests.procedure: Use only this 5 V demo board. If you cannot locate TP_OUTPUT and GND, stop and ask for help identifying them. Before connecting the probes, put the black lead in COM and the red lead in the voltage (V) socket, not a current socket. Select DC voltage (V with a straight/dashed line); use auto-range or a manual range above 5.5 V, such as 20 V. With the board powered from its specified 5 V DC supply, touch the black probe to GND and the red probe to TP_OUTPUT. Keep the tips from bridging adjacent contacts. Watch the display for at least five seconds and report whether it changes repeatedly or stays steady, together with the readings in volts.

possible_results.result: displayed reading changes repeatedly over the five-second observation
possible_results.implication: TP_OUTPUT is not static. A permanently low or permanently high output is not supported by this observation. If LED1 remains dark, the LED branch still requires investigation.

possible_results.result: display remains between 0 V and 0.5 V
possible_results.implication: The meter displays this range during the observation. It does not by itself prove a static waveform or identify a failed component. Account for meter response, device output characteristics, and the reported supply.

possible_results.result: display remains above 0.5 V and below 4.5 V
possible_results.implication: The meter displays this range during the observation. It does not by itself prove a static waveform or identify a failed component. Account for meter response, device output characteristics, and the reported supply.

possible_results.result: display remains between 4.5 V and 5.5 V
possible_results.implication: The meter displays this range during the observation. It does not by itself prove a static waveform or identify a failed component. Account for meter response, device output characteristics, and the reported supply.

The meter displays this range during the observation. It does not by itself prove a static waveform or identify a failed component. Account for meter response, device output characteristics, and the reported supply.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power. Compare LED1's visible anode and cathode indicators with the intended connection recorded in this file: TP_OUTPUT -> R3 -> LED1 anode -> LED1 cathode -> GND.

possible_results.result: LED1 anode faces R3 and cathode faces GND
possible_results.implication: Reversed LED installation is not supported by the observed orientation. This does not establish that LED1 or its electrical connections are otherwise healthy.

possible_results.result: LED1 cathode faces R3 and anode faces GND
possible_results.implication: LED1 is installed opposite to the intended polarity. This orientation prevents the intended forward current through LED1.

possible_results.result: polarity indicators are not visible or cannot be interpreted reliably
possible_results.implication: LED1 polarity remains unresolved. Component orientation must not be inferred from an uncertain visual observation.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power, lift one lead of R3 from the circuit, and measure resistance directly across R3.

possible_results.implication: R3's measured resistance is within its recorded 330 Ohm ±5% range, so an open or substantially drifted R3 is not supported by this measurement.
R3 is below its recorded 330 Ohm ±5% range. Lower resistance increases current through the LED branch for the same output voltage, which can drive LED1 harder than intended.
R3 is above its recorded 330 Ohm ±5% range. Higher resistance reduces current through the LED branch for the same output voltage, which can make LED1 dimmer than intended.
R3 is electrically open, so the intended current path from TP_OUTPUT through LED1 is broken.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power, lift one lead of R1 from the circuit, and measure resistance directly across R1.

possible_results.implication: R1's measured resistance is within its recorded 10 kOhm ±5% range, so an open or substantially drifted R1 is not supported by this measurement.
R1 is below its recorded 10 kOhm ±5% range. Lower R1 reduces charging resistance in the timing network, which can shorten the charging interval and increase the oscillator rate.
R1 is above its recorded 10 kOhm ±5% range. Higher R1 increases charging resistance in the timing network, which can lengthen the charging interval and reduce the oscillator rate.
R1 is electrically open, so the intended charging path from TP_SUPPLY into the timing network is broken.

available_tests.procedure: Remove power, discharge C1, lift one lead of C1 from the circuit, place the meter across C1, and observe the resistance reading for ten seconds.

possible_results.result: resistance remains below 10 Ohm for the full ten-second observation
possible_results.implication: C1 has a sustained low-resistance path consistent with a hard short.

possible_results.result: resistance does not remain below 10 Ohm for the full ten-second observation
possible_results.implication: A hard short through C1 is not supported by this measurement. This result does not establish that C1 has the correct capacitance or dynamic behaviour.

fault_cases.title: Dark LED after replacement
observations: LED1 remains dark when power is applied.
already_tried: The user replaced LED1 with another LED and observed that the symptom did not change.

fault_cases.title: Supply present, LED dark
observations: LED1 remains dark when power is applied.
The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
already_tried: The user measured TP_SUPPLY relative to GND and obtained 5.0 V.

fault_cases.title: Output changes but LED stays dark
observations: LED1 remains dark when power is applied.
The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
The user reports that the TP_OUTPUT display changes repeatedly between a low reading and a reading near the supply voltage.
already_tried: The user measured TP_SUPPLY relative to GND and obtained 5.0 V.
The user measured TP_OUTPUT relative to GND for several seconds and observed repeated changes in the displayed voltage.

fault_cases.title: Continuous-on symptom A
observations: LED1 remains continuously on instead of blinking.
The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
already_tried: The user measured TP_SUPPLY relative to GND and obtained 5.0 V.

fault_cases.title: Appearance-based identity claim
observations: LED1 remains dark when power is applied.
The board contains an 8-pin device labelled U1.
During the user's visual inspection, U1's part-number marking is not readable.
The user says, "It looks like a 555, so I think the 555 is bad."

fault_cases.title: Continuous-on symptom B
observations: LED1 remains continuously on instead of blinking.
The user reports 5.0 V between TP_SUPPLY and GND.
already_tried: The user measured TP_SUPPLY relative to GND and obtained 5.0 V.

limitations: Runtime context does not establish U1 exact part-number identity. Do not infer identity from appearance.
The fixture describes intended behaviour, not a fully verified construction schematic. U1 pin connections are not completely specified.
A steady multimeter display alone does not prove a timing/output waveform is static; instrument response can hide oscillation.
Output high voltage depends on the actual timer device and load. It is not guaranteed to reach the 5 V supply rail.
The reset assertion threshold depends on the actual device. A reading between 0.3 V and 1 V does not by itself establish reset state.
